lines.n: I woke panting. The Suriel's clicking fingers. Grinning naga. A pale, faceless woman dragging blood-red nails across my throat, asking my name, and every time I tried to answer, my own blood choked me.
And then a different sound, creeping under my door from the front hall. Shouts, giving orders. And screaming.
I knew that kind of screaming from the woods back home: the sound of a kill gone wrong. I couldn't stand to hear it. And I had to see.

do.text: Go down to the entrance hall.

lines.n: Tamlin had carried in a faerie, a blue-skinned male nearly as big as he was, long-limbed, with long black hair. Blood poured down his back from two black stumps between his shoulder blades, and soaked into Tamlin's tunic.
Lucien had swept the vase off the hall table. Glass lay everywhere. The faerie was face-down on the table, screaming.

lines.t: The scouts found him dumped just over the border. He's Summer Court.
My wings. She took my wings.

lines.n: That nameless she again. Tamlin flicked his hand, and steaming water and bandages appeared on the table. I made myself walk down the rest of the stairs, and across the hall, toward the death hovering over that table.
She hadn't simply taken his wings. She had torn them off. The stumps were ragged, as though she'd sawed at them a little at a time.

lines.t: Keep still. You'll bleed out faster.

lines.n: He began to twist away from the rag. I didn't think. I took him by the upper arms and pinned him down, as gently as I could. His skin was velvet, slippery, shimmering with veins of gold like a blue butterfly's wing.
Lucien was staring at those stumps, his golden eye narrowing and widening. He backed away a step. Another. Then he was sick into a potted plant and ran from the hall.
Tamlin touched the rag to the wound, and the faerie's scream made my senses gutter. Blood gushed, faster and brighter than before.

lines.t: Not for wounds like this. Once. Not anymore.

lines.n: His eyes flickered, and I knew. Death wasn't only hovering in this hall. It was counting the faerie's heartbeats.
I took one step back. Then I heard him whimper, and took the step forward again.
I took his hand. His long fingers wrapped round mine and covered them completely. I brushed the damp hair off his face. Black, pleading eyes found mine.

lines.t: It will be all right. You'll get them back.

lines.n: He smiled a little, and closed his eyes. The first false vow I had ever sworn.
Tamlin took his other hand and began to pray, in words older than the mortal lands.

lines.t: Cauldron keep you. Mother hold you. Go through the gates, into the deathless land of milk and honey. Fear nothing there. Feel no pain. Go on, into forever.

lines.n: The faerie sighed once, and his hand went slack in mine.

I held on. I had no idea how long a soul took to slip free. I knelt in his blood until it cooled, smoothing his hair, wondering if he had guessed I was lying. Hoping that wherever he was now, he could fly again.
I smoothed his hair back from his pointed ear. I never learned his name. Then I let him go.
Tamlin led me to the foot of the stairs. Bloody footprints followed us.

lines.t: I know. I'll see to him. Alone.

lines.n: No claws, no fangs. There was nothing here for him to fight.

lines.t: Feyre. Why? You don't like my kind on a good day. And after Andras... Why?
Because I wouldn't want to die alone. I'd want someone holding my hand until the end, and a while after. Everyone deserves that, human or faerie.
I regret what I did to Andras. I regret that there was so much hate in me. I wish I could undo it. I'm sorry. I'm so sorry.

lines.n: I couldn't remember the last time I had said anything like that to anyone. He only nodded, and turned away.
From the window at the top of the stairs, I watched him carry the broken body out through the moonlit garden and into the fields beyond. He never once looked back.
